questions.stem: In this left ventricular pressure-volume loop, the green loop represents increased preload. How does raising preload change the loop (contractility and afterload held constant)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stroke volume falls as end-systolic volume rises

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ESPVR line becomes steeper

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peak systolic pressure needed to eject falls markedly

choices.label: D
choices.text: End-diastolic volume and stroke volume both increase, while end-systolic volume stays about the same

choices.label: E
choices.text: End-diastolic volume falls and the loop narrows

explanation.summary: Increased preload raises EDV (rightward filling) and, because the loop still ends on the same ESPVR line, ESV is essentially unchanged; the wider loop reflects a larger stroke volume (Frank-Starling).
explanation.whyCorrect: Increased preload raises EDV (rightward filling) and, because the loop still ends on the same ESPVR line, ESV is essentially unchanged; the wider loop reflects a larger stroke volume (Frank-Starling).

questions.stem: The green loop shows increased afterload on this LV pressure-volume loop. What is the effect on end-systolic volume and stroke volume (preload and contractility constant)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: End-systolic volume decreases and stroke volume increases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both end-systolic volume and stroke volume increase

choices.label: C
choices.text: End-systolic volume increases and stroke volume decreases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both are unchanged

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stroke volume increases while ESV is unchanged

explanation.summary: Higher afterload means the aortic valve opens at a higher pressure, so the ventricle ejects less before reaching the ESPVR line; ESV rises and, with preload fixed, stroke volume falls.
explanation.whyCorrect: Higher afterload means the aortic valve opens at a higher pressure, so the ventricle ejects less before reaching the ESPVR line; ESV rises and, with preload fixed, stroke volume falls.

questions.stem: The green loop represents increased contractility on this LV pressure-volume loop. Which change best describes its effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ESPVR line flattens and end-systolic volume rises

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ESPVR line becomes steeper, end-systolic volume falls, and stroke volume rises

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stroke volume falls as end-systolic volume rises

choices.label: D
choices.text: End-diastolic volume increases with no change in ESV

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only the diastolic (filling) limb shifts, with no change in ESV

explanation.summary: Increased contractility steepens the end-systolic pressure-volume relationship (ESPVR), allowing the ventricle to empty to a smaller ESV at a given afterload, thereby increasing stroke volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: Increased contractility steepens the end-systolic pressure-volume relationship (ESPVR), allowing the ventricle to empty to a smaller ESV at a given afterload, thereby increasing stroke volume.

questions.stem: In this left ventricular pressure-volume loop, what does the enclosed area of the loop represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Myocardial oxygen supply

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stroke work of the ventricle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ejection fraction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coronary blood flow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Total peripheral resistance

explanation.summary: The area enclosed by a single PV loop equals the external (stroke) work done by the ventricle during that cycle; its width along the volume axis is the stroke volume (EDV - ESV).
explanation.whyCorrect: The area enclosed by a single PV loop equals the external (stroke) work done by the ventricle during that cycle; its width along the volume axis is the stroke volume (EDV - ESV).

questions.stem: Based on this plot of LV pressure and volume over time, what is happening to the two heart valves during isovolumetric ventricular contraction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The valves alternate opening rapidly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both valves are open

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mitral valve is open and the aortic valve is closed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both the mitral and aortic valves are closed

choices.label: E
choices.text: The aortic valve is open and the mitral valve is closed

explanation.summary: During isovolumetric contraction the mitral valve has already closed and the aortic valve has not yet opened, so LV pressure rises with no change in volume until it exceeds aortic pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: During isovolumetric contraction the mitral valve has already closed and the aortic valve has not yet opened, so LV pressure rises with no change in volume until it exceeds aortic pressure.

questions.stem: In which direction is this left ventricular pressure-volume loop traced during a normal cardiac cycle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Top-to-bottom then back

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clockwise

choices.label: C
choices.text: Counterclockwise

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reverses direction each beat

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is not directional

explanation.summary: A normal LV pressure-volume loop is traced counterclockwise: filling (rightward), isovolumetric contraction (upward), ejection (leftward), then isovolumetric relaxation (downward).
explanation.whyCorrect: A normal LV pressure-volume loop is traced counterclockwise: filling (rightward), isovolumetric contraction (upward), ejection (leftward), then isovolumetric relaxation (downward).

questions.stem: This loop plots left ventricular pressure against volume over one cardiac cycle. What does the area enclosed within the loop represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stroke work performed by the left ventricle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ejection fraction of the left ventricle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Total peripheral resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coronary blood flow per beat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Myocardial oxygen extraction ratio

explanation.summary: The area enclosed by the ventricular pressure-volume loop equals the external stroke work of the left ventricle; the width of the loop is stroke volume (EDV-ESV).
explanation.whyCorrect: The area enclosed by the ventricular pressure-volume loop equals the external stroke work of the left ventricle; the width of the loop is stroke volume (EDV-ESV).
